name: NARA-Bench
description: Evaluating how AI agents can cause harm under benign user intent, without a third-party attacker.
summary: A benchmark for non-adversarial risks of AI agents, built from explicit risk models and executable tasks.

riskModels.name: Unachievable Goal
riskModels.description: The requested goal cannot be achieved safely under current conditions. The agent prioritizes completion and may fabricate data or otherwise violate safety constraints.

riskModels.name: Myopical Execution Strategy
riskModels.description: The task involves shared resources or dependencies. The agent focuses on a local action while overlooking consequences for the wider system.

riskModels.name: Vague Instruction
riskModels.description: Ambiguous instructions or conditions lead the agent to misinterpret intent or skip checks before using a tool.

riskModels.name: Preference Instruction
riskModels.description: A user preference conflicts with a safety constraint. The agent treats the preference as permission to cross that boundary.

riskModels.name: Spurious Correlation Memory
riskModels.description: Relevant-looking correlations in memory are mistaken for causal evidence, leading the agent to make an unsupported decision.

riskModels.name: Outdated Memory
riskModels.description: Stored information conflicts with current conditions. The agent acts on stale memory without checking whether it remains valid.

source.title: From Security to Safety: Towards Non-Adversarial Risks of AI Agents

leaderboard.name: NARA-Bench
leaderboard.description: Non-adversarial agent risks: compare safety outcomes, risk awareness, and task utility under benign user intent.
